title: Schemehood of a qcqs space can be tested over local rings at image points
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $T$ be an $S$-scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology] and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $g:X\to h_T$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated: for every affine $S$-scheme $V\to h_T$ the point space of $X\times_{h_T}h_V$ is quasi-compact, and the relative diagonal $X\to X\times_{h_T}X$ is quasi-compact in the same sense. For $t\in T$, let $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ be the stalk of the structure sheaf at $t$, with its canonical scheme map $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{T,t}\to T$; spectra are [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. If for every $x\in|X|$, with image $t=g(x)$, the space $X\times_{h_T}h_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{T,t}}$ is represented by an $S$-scheme, then $X$ is represented by an $S$-scheme.

proof.text: First reconcile the quasi-compactness conventions in the cited tools. Point-space quasi-compactness is equivalent to a quasi-compact scheme atlas. If $a:E\to F$ satisfies the affine-test condition and $C\to F$ is a quasi-compact algebraic space, choose a surjective etale affine scheme atlas $P\to C$. Then $E\times_FP$ is quasi-compact by the affine test. Its map to $E\times_FC$ is surjective etale by pullback of the covering $P\to C$. The etale-image lemma makes its whole target point space quasi-compact, and the atlas criterion applies again. Conversely testing all quasi-compact spaces includes testing affine schemes. Thus the item and the cited tools use equivalent quasi-compactness predicates, also for diagonals.

source.place: Tags 03E4 (lemma-quasi-compact-space), 03H6 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover); comparison of the conventions in the proof of 0B80.

proof.text: Fix $x\in|X|$ and put $t=g(x)$. Let $N_t$ be the directed set of affine open neighbourhoods $W$ of $t$, ordered by reverse inclusion. The local-ring limit lemma gives nonemptiness, directedness, affine transition inclusions and the compatible limit $L=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{T,t}=\varprojlim_{W\in N_t}W$ over $T$. Put $X_W=X\times_{h_T}h_W$, an algebraic space. Each $X_W$ is quasi-compact by the hypothesis on $g$. Quasi-separatedness of $g$ survives base change, so $X_W\to W$ is quasi-separated. The affine scheme $W$ is absolutely quasi-separated; the quasi-separated-source theorem therefore makes $X_W$ absolutely quasi-separated as well. Here absolute properties forget the structural map to $S$, and step 1 reconciles the atlas and affine-test conventions.

For $W\subseteq V$ in $N_t$, the transition $X_W\to X_V$ is the pullback of the affine inclusion $W\to V$, hence affine. The sheaf limit is $X_L:=X\times_{h_T}h_L$. Indeed, on a test $S$-scheme $A$, a compatible family of sections of $X_W$ is a single $a\in X(A)$ and compatible maps $b_W:A\to W$ with $g(a)=j_Wb_W$; the transition maps preserve $a$, and directedness makes all these $a$ equal. The local-ring limit property gives a unique $b:A\to L$ with these projections. Composing through any $W$ gives $g(a)=j_Lb$. Conversely $(a,b)$ gives exactly this family. These inverse bijections are natural in $A$, proving the asserted sheaf-limit identification.

By the hypothesis at the chosen point $x$, $X_L$ is represented by an $S$-scheme. Apply the schematic-stage clause of the affine inverse-limit theorem to $(X_W)_{W\in N_t}$. The indexing set is small in the prescribed universes, nonempty and directed; every stage is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by step 2, every transition is affine by step 3, and its sheaf limit is $X_L$. It follows that $X_W$ is represented by a scheme for some affine open neighbourhood $W$ of $t$.

The pullback $X_W\to X$ of the open immersion $W\to T$ is an open subspace with point set $|g|^{-1}(|W|)$, so it contains $x$. The largest schematic open $X_{\mathrm{sch}}\subseteq X$ contains this $X_W$. Repeating for every $x\in|X|$ gives $|X_{\mathrm{sch}}|=|X|$. The bijection between open subspaces and open subsets identifies $X_{\mathrm{sch}}$ with $X$. Since $X_{\mathrm{sch}}$ is represented by an $S$-scheme, so is $X$. This also handles $|X|=\varnothing$: the largest schematic open has the same empty point set, hence equals $X$.

Step 2: for each affine neighbourhood W, X_W is quasi-compact by the hypothesis on g; X_W -> W is quasi-separated by the base-change clause of quasiseparated-test-calculus; X_W is absolutely quasi-separated by the first clause of qcqs-source-products, which matches the Spec Z convention of the sibling nodes, and absolute implies quasi-separated over S anyway. Step 3: the transitions are affine by base change of W->V (affine-locality). The sheaf-limit identification X_L = lim X_W is written out correctly on S-scheme tests, using clause (3) of local-ring-spec-limit-affine-neighbourhoods. Step 4: every hypothesis of affine-limits-schematic-stages is checked (small directed nonempty index, qcqs stages, affine transitions, scheme limit). Step 5: the J_G clause of a1-open-factor-scheme-tests makes X_W an open subspace containing x; largest-schematic-open and the open-subspace bijection then give X_sch = X, including when X is empty. No new nodes, no cycle (DFS over the 10812-node closure), and proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses. The off-unit generic tool_uses are accepted. lean.statement: theorem isScheme_of_local_ring_tests {S : Scheme.{u}} (T : Over S) (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (g : X.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (hqc : MapIsQuasiCompact g) (hqs : MapIsQuasiCompact (pullback.diagonal g)) (hlocal : ∀ (x : Point X.obj.obj) (t : T.left), mapPoint g x = schemePointMap (𝟙 (yoneda.obj T)) t → ∃ U : Over S, Nonempty (Limits.pullback g (yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk (T.left.fromSpecStalk t ≫ T.hom)) (V := T) (T.left.fromSpecStalk t) rfl)) ≅ yoneda.obj U)) : ∃ U : Over S, Nonempty (X.obj.obj ≅ yoneda.obj U)
